title: Mid-Autumn Festival
summary: A family gathered beneath the moon: harvest, gratitude and reunion.

title: Halloween
summary: Play, hospitality, unease and remembrance at the threshold of winter.

title: Bonfire Night
summary: The history beneath an autumn evening of bonfires and fireworks.

title: Diwali
summary: Lamps, homecoming and the many meanings of a shared season.

title: Remembrance Sunday
summary: A national pause to honour service and sacrifice, on the Sunday set aside for remembrance.

title: Indigenous Veterans Day
summary: Canada’s day of honour for First Nations, Inuit and Métis veterans, and for what they were denied.

title: Intersex Day of Solidarity
summary: A day of remembrance and solidarity, marked on the birthday of Herculine Barbin.

title: Synaxis of the Archangel Michael
summary: An Orthodox feast honouring the archangels and the other heavenly powers.

title: Victory Day (Azerbaijan)
summary: Azerbaijan’s national holiday marking the recapture of Shusha on 8 November 2020.

title: World Radiography Day
summary: The anniversary of the X-ray, and a thank-you to the people who use it to see inside the body.

title: World Town Planning Day
summary: A day for the quiet craft of making places that people can live in well.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
summary: The anniversary of 9 November 1989, when East Germany’s border opened after 28 years and the Cold War’s sharpest symbol began to fall.

title: Kristallnacht
summary: The anniversary of the November 1938 pogrom across Nazi Germany, a turning point on the road to the Holocaust.

title: Independence Day (Cambodia)
summary: Cambodia’s national holiday for its 1953 independence from France.

title: Amavasya (new moon day, Diwali week)
summary: The new moon day that runs until midday in New Delhi, the gap day between Diwali and Govardhan Puja this year.

title: Govardhan Puja (Annakut)
summary: The fourth day of Diwali, when Hindus offer a “mountain of food” to Krishna for lifting Govardhan Hill.

title: Atatürk Memorial Day (Turkey)
summary: Turkey falls silent at 09:05 to remember Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, who died at that minute on 10 November 1938.

title: World Science Day for Peace and Development
summary: UNESCO’s yearly day for science in society; the 2026 theme is “Common ground through science diplomacy”.

title: Bestu Varas (Gujarati New Year)
summary: The Gujarati New Year, opening Vikram Samvat 2083 the day after Diwali’s gap day.

title: US Marine Corps Birthday
summary: The 251st birthday of the US Marine Corps, founded by the Continental Congress on 10 November 1775.

title: Sesame Street’s birthday
summary: Sesame Street first aired on 10 November 1969; it turns 57 today.

title: Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald
summary: The 51st anniversary of the Lake Superior shipwreck that took 29 lives and inspired Gordon Lightfoot’s ballad.

title: Armistice Day (Remembrance Day)
summary: At 11am the UK and Commonwealth keep two minutes’ silence, 108 years after the guns of the First World War fell quiet.

title: Veterans Day (United States)
summary: America’s federal holiday honouring everyone who has served in its armed forces, born from Armistice Day.

title: Polish National Independence Day
summary: Poland celebrates regaining its independence on 11 November 1918, after 123 years wiped off the map.

title: Bhai Dooj
summary: The last day of Diwali, when sisters mark a tilak on their brothers’ foreheads and pray for their long life.

title: St Martin’s Day (Martinmas)
summary: The feast of St Martin of Tours: lantern processions, roast goose and, once, the end of the farming year.

title: Carnival season opens at 11:11 (Germany)
summary: At 11:11 on 11.11, Cologne, Düsseldorf and Mainz kick off the “fifth season” of carnival.

title: Singles’ Day (China)
summary: China’s tongue-in-cheek day for the unattached, born at Nanjing University in 1993, now the world’s biggest shopping festival.

title: Angola Independence Day
summary: Angola marks 51 years since Agostinho Neto proclaimed independence from Portugal on 11 November 1975.

title: World Pneumonia Day
summary: A global day of action against pneumonia, the world’s biggest infectious killer of children and a major threat to older adults, held every 12 November since 2009.

title: Dr Sun Yat-sen’s Birthday (Taiwan)
summary: Taiwan remembers the doctor-turned-revolutionary born on 12 November 1866, ‘Father of the Nation’ of the Republic of China; the date is also Chinese Cultural Renaissance Day and Doctors’ Day.

title: Anniversary of the World Wide Web proposal (1990)
summary: On 12 November 1990 Tim Berners-Lee and Robert Cailliau put forward the formal proposal at CERN that gave the World Wide Web its name.

title: Scott’s polar party found (1912)
summary: On 12 November 1912 a search party found the snow-covered tent holding the bodies of Captain Scott, Edward Wilson and Henry Bowers on the Antarctic ice.

title: Voyager 1 at Saturn (1980)
summary: On 12 November 1980 Voyager 1 swept past Titan and made its closest approach to Saturn, revealing braided rings, new moons and Titan’s orange haze.

title: Philae lands on a comet (2014)
summary: On 12 November 2014 the European Space Agency’s Philae lander made the first ever touchdown on a comet, then bounced across its surface before coming to rest in the shadows.

title: Public Service Broadcasting Day (India)
summary: India remembers Mahatma Gandhi’s only visit to the All India Radio studios, on 12 November 1947, when he spoke to Partition refugees at Kurukshetra.

title: BBC Children in Need Appeal Night
summary: The BBC’s own children’s charity holds its 47th appeal night, a three-hour live telethon from Salford with Pudsey Bear, a nationwide children’s choir and landmarks lit up yellow.

title: World Kindness Day
summary: Held every 13 November since 1998, when the first World Kindness Movement conference opened in Tokyo, a day for small good deeds that cross borders, faiths and cultures.

title: Martyrdom of Fatimah al-Zahra (Iran)
summary: Iran’s national day of mourning for Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad, on 3 Jumada al-Thani, the high point of the Shia Fatimiyya season; the date follows the lunar calendar and can shift by a day.

title: Wangala, the Hundred Drums Festival
summary: The Garo people’s post-harvest thanksgiving to the sun god Misi Saljong, a public holiday in Meghalaya, India, today, with this year’s big celebration planned around 1,000 drums.

title: Friday the 13th
summary: The third and last Friday the 13th of 2026, a rare three-in-a-year run, and a look at where the superstition really comes from.

title: Robert Louis Stevenson born (1850)
summary: The author of Treasure Island, Kidnapped and Jekyll and Hyde was born in Edinburgh on 13 November 1850, 176 years ago today.

title: World Diabetes Day
summary: Held every 14 November on the birthday of Frederick Banting, co-discoverer of insulin, the world's largest diabetes awareness campaign. The 2026 theme is “Early action on diabetes”.

title: Moby-Dick published in America (1851)
summary: On 14 November 1851 Harper & Brothers published Herman Melville's Moby-Dick in New York, 175 years ago today. It sold poorly, then became one of the great novels in English.

title: Children’s Day (Bal Diwas), India
summary: India celebrates its children every 14 November, the birthday of its first prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru, born in 1889 and fondly known as Chacha Nehru.

title: Chhath Puja: Kharna
summary: Day two of the four-day Hindu festival of Chhath, devoted to the Sun god and Chhathi Maiya. After a day's fast, devotees eat a sweet kheer at dusk and then begin a 36-hour fast without water.

title: The King’s birthday
summary: King Charles III was born at Buckingham Palace on 14 November 1948 and turns 78 today, an official flag-flying day on UK government buildings.

title: The Coventry Blitz (1940)
summary: On the night of 14 to 15 November 1940, German bombers devastated Coventry in an 11-hour raid that destroyed its medieval cathedral and gave birth to a lasting ministry of reconciliation.

title: Claude Monet born (1840)
summary: The father of Impressionism was born in Paris on 14 November 1840, 186 years ago today, in the year that also marks the centenary of his death.

title: Chhath Puja: Sandhya Arghya
summary: On the third and greatest day of Chhath Puja, millions stand in rivers and ponds across Bihar, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Nepal to offer water and gifts to the setting sun.

title: World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims
summary: On the third Sunday of November, the world remembers everyone killed or injured on the roads. The day began in Britain in 1993 with a bereaved mother's charity, RoadPeace.

title: Shichi-Go-San (Japan)
summary: Japan's "seven-five-three" festival, when children of three, five and seven are dressed in kimono and taken to Shinto shrines to give thanks for their healthy growth.

title: Proclamation of the Republic (Brazil)
summary: Brazil's national holiday marks 15 November 1889, when a military coup in Rio de Janeiro ended the Empire of Brazil and sent Emperor Pedro II into exile.

title: King's Feast (Belgium)
summary: Belgium's Fête du Roi, held every 15 November since 1866, honours the monarch with a Te Deum in Brussels, a ceremony in Parliament and, by curious tradition, without the King himself.

title: Day of the Imprisoned Writer
summary: Since 1981, PEN International has used 15 November to stand with writers jailed, silenced or disappeared for their words. This year it highlights five writers from Vietnam, Cuba, the UAE, Belarus and Rwanda.

title: Nativity Fast begins (Eastern Christianity)
summary: Today many Orthodox and Eastern Catholic Christians begin the 40-day Nativity Fast, or Winter Lent, in preparation for Christmas. It starts the day after the feast of St Philip, so it is also called Philip's Fast.

title: The First Salute: Statia Day at 250
summary: 250 years ago today, the guns of Fort Oranje on the tiny Dutch Caribbean island of St Eustatius answered the salute of an American warship, the first time a foreign fort is said to have honoured the new United States. Today King Willem-Alexander joins the island for the anniversary.

title: International Day for Tolerance
summary: Every 16 November the UN and UNESCO mark the International Day for Tolerance, born from a declaration UNESCO adopted on its 50th birthday in 1995. The date also marks 81 years since UNESCO's constitution was signed in London.

title: Chhath Puja: Usha Arghya
summary: At dawn today devotees across Bihar, eastern India, Nepal and the diaspora stood in rivers and ponds to offer water to the rising sun, ending the four-day Chhath festival and its 36-hour waterless fast.

title: Icelandic Language Day
summary: Iceland celebrates its language every 16 November, the birthday of the poet and naturalist Jónas Hallgrímsson, who coined words such as reikistjarna, a 'wandering star', for planet.

title: Battle of Fort Washington, 250 years on
summary: On 16 November 1776 British and Hessian troops stormed Fort Washington at the top of Manhattan and captured almost 2,900 Americans, one of the Continental Army's worst defeats. Washington Heights is marking the 250th anniversary.

title: Estonia's Day of Declaration of Sovereignty
summary: On 16 November 1988 Estonia's Soviet-era parliament declared that its own laws outranked those of the USSR, the first legislative step towards restoring independence. Estonia marks it as a day of national importance.

title: International Students’ Day and the Day of Struggle for Freedom and Democracy
summary: Every 17 November students worldwide remember the Czech students the Nazis seized and shot in Prague in 1939, and Czechs and Slovaks mark the same date as the day the 1989 Velvet Revolution began, 50 years later to the day.

title: World Cervical Cancer Elimination Day
summary: The second-ever World Cervical Cancer Elimination Day, set by the World Health Assembly in 2025 on the anniversary of WHO’s 2020 pledge to make cervical cancer the first cancer the world eliminates. The date now belongs to it, so World Prematurity Day has moved to 15 November.

title: Polytechneio: the Athens Polytechnic Uprising
summary: Greece remembers the November 1973 student uprising at the Athens Polytechnic, crushed when a junta tank broke through the gates in the small hours of 17 November. Today is the 53rd anniversary, a school holiday ending in the traditional march to the US Embassy.

title: Queene’s Day: Elizabeth I’s Accession Day
summary: On 17 November 1558 Elizabeth I became queen, and for centuries afterwards England celebrated the date with bells, bonfires, jousts and burning effigies of the Pope. It is all but forgotten now, except in one Devon village that revived it in 2005.

title: The Suez Canal Opens
summary: On 17 November 1869 a flotilla led by the French imperial yacht L’Aigle, with Empress Eugénie aboard, sailed into the Suez Canal and joined the Mediterranean to the Red Sea. Today is the 157th anniversary of one of the great engineering openings of the 19th century.

title: Homemade Bread Day
summary: A small, cosy American observance from the early 1980s, started by a group in Ann Arbor, Michigan, to get families baking their own loaves. A good excuse to fill the kitchen with the smell of bread on a November evening.

title: Proclamation Day of the Republic of Latvia
summary: Latvia’s national day marks the 108th anniversary of the proclamation of the Republic of Latvia in Riga on 18 November 1918, with a military parade, candles in windows and concerts at the Freedom Monument.

title: Morocco’s Independence Day
summary: Morocco’s Independence Day commemorates the announcement Sultan Mohammed V made on 18 November 1955, two days after he returned from exile, declaring the end of the protectorate era.

title: Vertières Day: Haiti’s Day of Army and Victory
summary: Haiti marks the 223rd anniversary of the Battle of Vertières on 18 November 1803, the victory that ended French rule in Saint-Domingue and opened the way to independence on 1 January 1804.

title: World Day for the Prevention of and Healing from Child Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Violence
summary: The United Nations’ 18 November World Day, created in 2022 and building on a Council of Europe day of 2015, is dedicated to preventing child sexual exploitation and abuse and to supporting survivors in healing.

title: World COPD Day
summary: The 25th World COPD Day, held on the third Wednesday of November, is themed “Early Diagnosis and Management for a Better Life,” and highlights a lung disease the WHO now ranks as the third leading cause of death worldwide.

title: European Antibiotic Awareness Day and World AMR Awareness Week
summary: 18 November is European Antibiotic Awareness Day and the start of WHO’s World AMR Awareness Week, running to 24 November, with the 2026 themes “Care for your kids – use antibiotics wisely” and “One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now.”

title: Mickey Mouse’s Birthday
summary: Mickey Mouse’s official 98th birthday marks the premiere of Steamboat Willie at New York’s Colony Theatre on 18 November 1928, the synchronised-sound cartoon that made Mickey, and Minnie, stars.

title: Croatia’s Day of Remembrance of the Victims of Vukovar and Škabrnja
summary: Croatia’s national remembrance day marks the 35th anniversary of the fall of Vukovar after an 87-day siege on 18 November 1991, and of the Škabrnja massacre on the same day.

title: Louis Daguerre’s Birthday
summary: The 239th anniversary of the birth of Louis-Jacques-Mandé Daguerre, born on 18 November 1787, the French painter and inventor of the daguerreotype, the first photographic process to come into wide use.

title: International Day of Islamic Art
summary: UNESCO’s International Day of Islamic Art, proclaimed in 2019 at Bahrain’s proposal and held every 18 November, celebrates historic and contemporary Islamic art and its place in world culture.

title: World Toilet Day
summary: Every 19 November the United Nations asks the world to talk about toilets, because 3.4 billion people still lack safe sanitation. The 2026 theme is sanitation and gender equality, under the slogan “Safe toilets. Equal futures.”

title: International Men’s Day
summary: Held every 19 November since it was revived in Trinidad and Tobago in 1999, International Men’s Day celebrates men and boys and puts a spotlight on their health and wellbeing. In the UK the 2026 theme is “Supporting Men and Boys”.

title: World Philosophy Day
summary: UNESCO’s day for philosophy falls on the third Thursday of November, which this year is 19 November. In Paris the Senegalese philosopher Souleymane Bachir Diagne gives the 2026 lecture, “Living the Earth Together”.

title: The Gettysburg Address
summary: On 19 November 1863 Abraham Lincoln rose at the dedication of the soldiers’ cemetery at Gettysburg and spoke for about two minutes. Today is the 163rd anniversary of what became one of the most famous speeches in history.

title: Monaco National Day
summary: Monaco celebrates its National Day, the Fête du Prince, every 19 November with a Te Deum, a parade in Palace Square and fireworks over the harbour. The date honours Saint Rainier and the accession of Prince Rainier III in 1949.

title: Garifuna Settlement Day
summary: Belize’s Garifuna Settlement Day, every 19 November, remembers the arrival of the largest group of Garifuna settlers, led by Alejo Beni, on 19 November 1823. It begins at dawn with Yurumein, a re-enactment of the landing by dugout canoe.

title: Día de la Puertorriqueñidad (Discovery of Puerto Rico Day)
summary: Puerto Rico’s 19 November holiday marks the arrival of Christopher Columbus’s fleet on 19 November 1493. Long called Discovery Day, it was renamed the Day of Puerto Ricanness in 2022 to honour the Taíno people who already lived on the island.

title: The Great American Smokeout
summary: On the third Thursday of every November the American Cancer Society asks smokers to quit for a day and make a plan to quit for good. Today, 19 November 2026, is the Smokeout’s 50th anniversary.

title: World Pancreatic Cancer Day
summary: On the third Thursday of November, this year 19 November, charities around the world turn landmarks purple to raise awareness of pancreatic cancer, one of the deadliest cancers. The day began in 2014; this is its 13th year.

title: Indira Gandhi’s Birth Anniversary and National Integration Day
summary: India marks the birth of Indira Gandhi, its first and only woman prime minister, born on 19 November 1917, as National Integration Day, or Qaumi Ekta Diwas. It opens a week of events on communal harmony and national unity.

title: Apollo 12: the second Moon landing
summary: On 19 November 1969 Apollo 12 landed in the Ocean of Storms. Its precision landing helped turn a remarkable first achievement into a programme of scientific exploration.

title: Brazil’s Flag Day
summary: Brazil marks the adoption of its republican flag on 19 November 1889. Its green, yellow, blue and white design combines political history with a carefully arranged starry sky.

title: The birthday of Charles I
summary: Charles I was born on 19 November 1600 in Dunfermline. His 426th birth anniversary opens a window onto the civil wars, royal power and an extraordinary art collection.

title: Women’s Entrepreneurship Day
summary: Held on 19 November, Women’s Entrepreneurship Day recognises women who build businesses and seeks to widen economic opportunity. The annual date is distinct from its New York summit, held on 13 November in 2026.

title: Social Enterprise Day
summary: Social Enterprise Day falls on 19 November in 2026, celebrating businesses that trade for a social or environmental purpose. In the UK, the campaign highlights their contribution to local communities.

title: National Rural Health Day (United States)
summary: America’s National Rural Health Day is held on the third Thursday of November. On 19 November 2026 it marks 15 years of recognising the people and organisations supporting rural healthcare.

title: World Children’s Day
summary: The anniversary of the UN’s 1959 children’s rights declaration and its 1989 Convention on the Rights of the Child. Today’s campaign asks adults to listen to children about their rights and futures.

title: Transgender Day of Remembrance
summary: A day to remember transgender people killed in acts of anti-transgender violence. It began with a vigil in 1999 and is marked through readings of names, gatherings and quiet remembrance.

title: Devutthana Ekadashi (Prabodhini Ekadashi)
summary: The Hindu observance of Vishnu’s awakening and the close of Chaturmas. London’s Drik Panchang places it on 20 November 2026; some traditions, including the BAPS calendar, observe it on 21 November.

title: Brazil’s Black Consciousness Day
summary: Brazil’s national holiday on 20 November remembers Zumbi dos Palmares and celebrates Black history, culture and resistance. In 2026 it is the 331st anniversary of Zumbi’s death.

title: The Mexican Revolution: 116 years on
summary: Mexico commemorates the uprising called for 20 November 1910 by Francisco I. Madero. The historical anniversary is today; the associated 2026 day off was observed on Monday 16 November.

title: Africa Industrialization Day
summary: The UN’s annual 20 November observance focuses on African industrial development, jobs and economic opportunity. The 2026 programme in Lusaka centres on financing inclusive and sustainable industrialisation.

title: Vietnamese Teachers’ Day
summary: Vietnam honours teachers every 20 November through school gatherings, visits and expressions of gratitude. The national observance was formally established in 1982, building on an earlier international teachers’ charter day.

title: Argentina’s National Sovereignty Day
summary: The 20 November anniversary remembers resistance to an Anglo-French fleet at Vuelta de Obligado in 1845. In 2026 the historical date is Friday; Argentina’s associated public holiday is Monday 23 November.

title: The opening of the Nuremberg trial
summary: On 20 November 1945 the International Military Tribunal opened the trial of leading Nazi officials. Eighty-one years later, the anniversary recalls a landmark effort to establish individual responsibility for international crimes.

title: The retreat from Fort Lee: 250 years on
summary: On 20 November 1776 British troops crossed the Hudson and forced the Americans to abandon Fort Lee. The 250th anniversary recalls a dangerous retreat that preserved Washington’s army for the fighting still ahead.

title: Edwin Hubble’s birthday
summary: Astronomer Edwin Hubble was born on 20 November 1889. His 137th birth anniversary recalls the observations that established other galaxies beyond the Milky Way and helped reveal an expanding universe.

title: Elizabeth and Philip’s wedding: 79 years on
summary: Princess Elizabeth married Philip Mountbatten at Westminster Abbey on 20 November 1947. The 79th anniversary recalls a postwar royal wedding preserved through its service, photographs and later commemorations.

title: World Television Day
summary: Thirty years after the first UN World Television Forum, a day to consider television’s power to inform, connect and shape public life.

title: Ukraine’s Day of Dignity and Freedom
summary: Ukraine’s annual 21 November commemoration honours the civic movements of 2004 and 2013–14 and the right to choose the country’s future.

title: Tulsi Vivah
summary: London’s Hindu calendar places the ceremonial marriage of Tulsi and Vishnu on 21 November 2026. Family and temple traditions may choose a different day within the festival period.

title: The Presentation of Mary and Pro Orantibus Day
summary: A feast of Mary’s dedication to God, known in Orthodox tradition as the Entry of the Theotokos into the Temple. Catholics also remember contemplative religious communities today.

title: World Fisheries Day
summary: An annual day for healthy waters and the people who depend on them. The 2026 FAO–ILO programme focuses on decent work, especially for young people and women.

title: World Hello Day
summary: An independent peace observance begun in 1973, inviting everyone to greet ten people and value personal communication.

title: International Survivors of Suicide Loss Day
summary: Held on the Saturday before US Thanksgiving, this day brings people bereaved by suicide together for remembrance, understanding and connection.

title: The Dayton Peace Accords: 31 years on
summary: On 21 November 1995 negotiators initialled the agreement that ended the Bosnian war. The anniversary recalls both a vital peace settlement and the difficult work of living together afterwards.

title: Bangladesh Armed Forces Day
summary: Bangladesh’s annual 21 November observance honours military service and the Liberation War. In 2026 it is 55 years since the wartime date commemorated by the armed forces.

title: Greece’s Armed Forces Day
summary: Greece honours its armed forces on 21 November, the feast of the Entry of the Theotokos. The 2026 programme includes worship, remembrance and a public open day.

title: The first free human balloon flight
summary: On 21 November 1783 two men flew freely over Paris in a Montgolfier balloon. The 243rd anniversary recalls a short journey that changed the possibilities of human travel.

title: Bloody Sunday in Dublin, 1920
summary: The 106th anniversary of a day of killings during Ireland’s War of Independence, including the deaths of fourteen people at Croke Park.

title: Voltaire’s birthday
summary: The conventional 21 November 1694 birth date of the French writer opens a window onto satire, tolerance and a lasting exchange of ideas with Britain.

title: Venice’s Feast of the Madonna della Salute
summary: Venetians cross a temporary bridge to give thanks and pray for health on 21 November, renewing a tradition born from the plague of 1630–31.

title: Rocky’s New York opening: 50 years on
summary: The American Film Institute dates Rocky’s New York opening to 21 November 1976. Fifty years later, its story of an unlikely contender remains part of film history.

title: National Adoption Day in the United States
summary: America’s National Adoption Day falls on 21 November 2026, bringing courts and communities together around adoption from foster care and children’s need for lasting families.

title: Christ the King
summary: The final Sunday of the Western church year celebrates Christ’s reign, before Advent begins on 29 November.

title: Lebanon Independence Day
summary: Lebanon marks 83 years since the release of its imprisoned leaders on 22 November 1943, a defining moment in independence from French mandate rule.

title: Albanian Alphabet Day
summary: A celebration of the Congress of Manastir, which met from 14 to 22 November 1908 and helped give written Albanian a common foundation.

title: Stir-up Sunday
summary: The Sunday before Advent brings an old prayer and the British custom of mixing Christmas pudding together; in 2026 it falls on 22 November.

title: Totensonntag (Eternity Sunday)
summary: Germany’s Protestant churches close the church year by remembering the dead and making room for grief and Christian hope.

title: St Cecilia’s Day
summary: The traditional feast of the patron saint of music honours musicians, while this year’s Sunday solemnity takes precedence in the Roman Catholic calendar.

title: Benjamin Britten born (1913)
summary: The Suffolk composer was born 113 years ago on St Cecilia’s Day, beginning a life that would reshape British opera and musical participation.

title: George Eliot born (1819)
summary: Born Mary Anne Evans near Nuneaton on 22 November 1819, the novelist behind Middlemarch is remembered on her 207th birthday anniversary.

title: World Youth Sunday
summary: Catholic parishes celebrate young people’s place in the Church on Christ the King Sunday, with England and Wales’s 2026 resources centred on St Francis.

title: John F. Kennedy assassinated (1963)
summary: The 63rd anniversary of Kennedy’s assassination in Dallas remembers a president’s death, a sudden transfer of power and an enduring public memory.

title: C. S. Lewis remembered (1963)
summary: The Narnia author and literary scholar died on 22 November 1963; his Westminster Abbey memorial was dedicated on the same date fifty years later.

title: Charles de Gaulle born (1890)
summary: De Gaulle was born in Lille on 22 November 1890; his 136th birth anniversary turns attention to his beginnings and the surviving records of them.

title: Mike Tyson’s first heavyweight title: 40 years
summary: On 22 November 1986, twenty-year-old Tyson stopped Trevor Berbick to win the WBC heavyweight title and become the youngest world heavyweight champion.

title: Blackbeard’s final battle (1718)
summary: The conventional anniversary of Blackbeard’s death at Ocracoke on 22 November 1718 opens a story of piracy, colonial power and evidence beneath the legend.

title: China Clipper’s Pacific airmail flight (1935)
summary: The flying boat left Alameda on 22 November 1935 to inaugurate trans-Pacific airmail service, linking California with Manila through island stops.

title: Ravi Pradosh Vrat (Pradosham)
summary: An evening observance dedicated to Shiva falls on Sunday 22 November in Indian calendars and in a published London temple programme; local dates and timings vary.

title: Labour Thanksgiving Day (Japan)
summary: Japan gives thanks for work and its fruits on 23 November, a modern public holiday with roots in an imperial harvest ritual.

title: Bon Om Touk: Cambodia’s Water Festival begins
summary: The Water Festival public holiday runs from 23 to 25 November 2026. The main Phnom Penh celebrations are suspended this year, while provincial observances may continue.

title: Giorgoba: St George’s Day in Georgia
summary: Georgia’s November feast of St George is a public holiday, marked by worship and gatherings on 23 November.

title: Tazaungdaing: Myanmar’s holiday period begins
summary: Myanmar’s Tazaungmone holiday period begins on 23 November 2026, ahead of the full-moon observance, with traditions of lights, giving and robe weaving.

title: Great March and Restoration Day (British Virgin Islands)
summary: The British Virgin Islands observes its 2026 public holiday for the Great March of 1949 and the restoration of the Legislative Council today; the march itself took place on 24 November.

title: Doctor Who first broadcast: 63 years on
summary: Doctor Who began on BBC television on 23 November 1963, opening a door from an ordinary London junkyard into an extraordinary universe.

title: Manuel de Falla’s 150th birthday
summary: Born in Cádiz on 23 November 1876, Manuel de Falla is remembered in a special anniversary year through performances, research and renewed listening.

title: Fibonacci Day
summary: The digits in 11/23 give 1, 1, 2, 3: an informal day for enjoying a famous number sequence, with educational celebrations in 2026.

title: St Clement’s Day
summary: The Western feast of Clement of Rome recalls an early Christian leader and a surviving letter concerned with peace in a divided community.

title: St Columbanus’s Day
summary: The Roman feast of the Irish monk Columbanus follows a trail from Bangor to monasteries in continental Europe and his final home at Bobbio.

title: Alexander Litvinenko’s death: 20 years on
summary: Twenty years after Alexander Litvinenko died in London on 23 November 2006, the anniversary recalls his family’s pursuit of answers and the official findings about his poisoning.

title: Navy Day in Mexico
summary: Mexico’s Navy Day recalls the Spanish evacuation of San Juan de Ulúa on 23 November 1825, a decisive step in consolidating independence at sea.

title: LIFE’s first photojournalism issue: 90 years
summary: The first issue of Henry Luce’s picture-led LIFE was dated 23 November 1936; ninety years later, the title has announced a new print issue for today.
